result:
I graded Riley's second attempt at quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`: three items correct, two partial and one wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes a request that names the tool and gives its arguments. This was wrong on the first attempt. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug". Repeating the same failing step 40 times means more steps add nothing, so the program needs a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right, but you said the model "runs" the tools. It only requests them, and the program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | "By the name" is only part of it. The model reads each tool's full description: its name, what it does and its parameters. |

**Summary:** Riley has the loop down and now sees that the model only requests tool calls. Two things are still open. The first is that the model never runs tools, which the q4 reasoning shows. The second is that an agent needs a stopping condition.

**Next step:** Riley should redo q3 and q6 from memory after re-reading the parts of the agent-loop lesson on stopping and on tool descriptions. After that, the next topic is context and memory.

I also added `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-who-runs-tools-and-when-to-stop.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I did not grade `s1`, because you asked only for `s2`. Say if you want it graded too.
